memory_candidates.content: When a batch/multi-task engine consolidates several dispatch sites into ONE call to a shared script (e.g. orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh), a plan's Scope Hypothesis grep pattern tuned for the single-task SKILL.md dispatch-site shape (build_args+=(--lit)) can miss the multi-task engine's own call site into that same script, which often uses a different shell idiom ($(... echo --lit) inside a single command substitution rather than a standalone build_args+=() line). Always separately check the multi-task/batch call site when threading a new flag through both single-task and multi-task orchestrate paths.

To live-test agent-authored bash logic embedded in a markdown agent/skill file without spawning a real subagent, extract the fenced ```bash block by matching a unique variable name inside it (e.g. via python re.findall on the file content), write it to a temp .sh file, then source it in a subshell with the same environment variables (delegation-context-style vars) the agent would have. This proves the exact shipped logic works against controlled fixtures, going beyond mere code-reading inspection, and is especially valuable when the full real toolchain (e.g. a Lean project + Comparator binaries) is unavailable or too costly to spin up during implementation.
